DURATION 15 SECONDS | HORIZONTAL 16:9

CHARACTER REFERENCES
{{CHAR_JAMSHID_WORKER}}
{{CHAR_ZAHHAK}}
{{CHAR_GUARDS}}

{{LOC_BALCONY}}

{{PROP_ZAHHAK_STAFF}}
{{PROP_INDUSTRIAL_SAW}}
{{PROP_RESTRAINTS}}
{{PROP_COLLECTION_OBJECTS}}

DIRECTION AND CONTINUITY
Create a 15-second horizontal 16:9 live-action cinematic sequence.

Preserve each referenced identity, costume, proportions and rigid handmade mask. Mask geometry and eye openings remain fixed. All visible humans wear their referenced masks.

Emotion comes from posture, hands, breath and visible eyes.

Each listed hard cut changes the physical camera station, lens or viewpoint.

Jamshid’s shots use close, unsettled handheld camerawork with brief focus slips that recover on essential action.

Zahhak’s shot uses a calm, controlled retreating camera at a slightly low angle.

References anchor design; written lighting controls illumination.

Zahhak remains unhurried and indifferent. Whenever he walks, the staff plants first, his weight transfers onto it, then his weaker leg follows in an uneven step. Preserve the weak-leg side established in the reference.

His two single-headed shoulder snakes remain alive, making small independent movements. Preserve their attachment, scale and proportions.

NO MUSIC.
NO DIALOGUE.

LOCATION AND LIGHT
Night in one vast collection hall with a continuous flat floor.

SOUTH: the main entrance.
NORTH: the doorway leading onto the balcony.
Along the perimeter walls: collection objects on low display furniture.
Immediately WEST of the north balcony doorway: the display table Zahhak has been examining.
CENTER: a functional industrial timber saw standing directly on the flat floor.

The machine is not on a pedestal and is not inside a separate room.

Its level feed carriage runs WEST to EAST toward the fixed blade at its EAST end. The controls are on its SOUTH side.

Cold integrated ceiling lights illuminate the interior. Small neutral display lights skim the perimeter objects. One harder neutral task lamp illuminates the saw.

Weak cool exterior spill enters through the NORTH balcony opening.

For the frontal shot of Zahhak, that opening is BEHIND THE CAMERA. Its light may reach his front, but the opening, balcony and exterior view remain outside the frame.

Keep illumination and exposure consistent across all shots.

START STATE AND BLOCKING
Jamshid is at the WEST head end of the central carriage.

Guard A controls his left shoulder.
Guard B controls his right side.

The carriage is stationary.
The blade at the EAST end is OFF.

Zahhak starts beside the NORTH display table, WEST of the balcony doorway. He leaves the display and follows the clear aisle toward the NORTH balcony.

He never turns toward Jamshid.

Jamshid’s gaze stays directed NORTH toward Zahhak’s position.

SHOT 10-01 | 0s–2s | 2 SECONDS
35mm close handheld from SOUTHWEST beside Jamshid.

The guards drag him the last step to the carriage.

His knees fail to support him and his gaze stays north, stunned at having been ignored.

The camera dips with him and briefly loses precise focus before recovering his eyes.

SHOT 10-02 | 2s–5s | 3 SECONDS
28mm oblique from SOUTH of the machine, showing the WEST carriage, Jamshid and the fixed EAST blade in one composition.

A and B force him into a seated position, then lower his back along the carriage.

His head points WEST.
His feet point EAST.

The WEST-to-EAST feed path toward the blade is visible.

No contact occurs.

The handheld camera physically edges closer.

SHOT 10-03 | 5s–9s | 4 SECONDS
32mm slightly low frontal full-body shot of Zahhak.

CAMERA POSITION:
The camera is NORTH of Zahhak, just inside the balcony doorway, looking SOUTH into the hall.

Zahhak faces NORTH toward the camera and walks toward the balcony.

The camera retreats NORTH ahead of him, maintaining its SOUTH-facing view.

SPATIAL ORDER:
Interior hall behind Zahhak.
Zahhak facing the camera.
Camera retreating ahead of Zahhak.
Balcony and exterior behind the camera, outside the image.

Keep Zahhak’s masked face, chest and the front of his costume visible.

Behind his body, show only the receding INTERIOR of the collection hall: interior columns, perimeter displays, objects and the flat floor under the established ceiling lights.

Do not place the sea, city, skyline, exterior sky, balcony railing or balcony opening behind Zahhak.

Do not reverse the camera into a rear view.
Do not orbit around him.
Do not turn him to face back into the hall.

Zahhak advances slowly:
his staff plants;
his weight settles onto it;
his weaker leg follows.

Keep his feet and staff tip visible enough to read the limp.

His eyes remain directed along his route toward the balcony beyond the camera. He never looks toward Jamshid or the machine.

His two shoulder snakes make subtle independent movements.

The camera retreats smoothly and unhurriedly, preserving the low frontal angle and the interior background throughout the entire shot.

End before a balcony railing or exterior view enters the frame.

SHOT 10-04 | 9s–11s | 2 SECONDS
50mm close from NORTHWEST of the carriage, beside Jamshid’s head.

A secures a broad hip strap.

Jamshid’s left forearm is held beside his torso.
His RIGHT arm remains free.

Jamshid continues staring toward the north display and balcony direction, breathing shallowly.

His dominant state is stunned disbelief at being ignored.

SHOT 10-05 | 11s–13s | 2 SECONDS
65mm close from SOUTH at the controls.

B operates the machine start control.

A remains beside Jamshid.

The motor engages.
The carriage remains stationary.

No instructional labels or readable text.

SHOT 10-06 | 13s–15s | 2 SECONDS
75mm tight oblique from SOUTHEAST of the blade housing.

The exposed cutting edge accelerates into its working motion.

Preserve the referenced blade mechanism exactly.

Metal vibration and the running drive are visible.

Jamshid remains outside this tight frame.

Cut before the carriage advances.

END STATE AND EDIT
The blade is RUNNING.
The carriage remains stationary.

Jamshid lies with his head WEST and feet EAST.
His hip strap is secured.
His RIGHT arm remains free.
His gaze points NORTH.

A remains beside his head.
B remains at the SOUTH controls.

Zahhak is approaching the NORTH balcony threshold.

In the last image of Zahhak, he was seen from the FRONT with the INTERIOR HALL behind him. The balcony was ahead of him and behind the camera.

Carry the running machine sound into the following sequence without restarting it.

SOUND
Dragging shoes.
Carriage creaks.
Strap friction.
Jamshid’s shallow breathing.

During Zahhak’s shot:
measured staff contacts;
slow uneven footsteps;
restrained costume movement.

At the machine:
start-switch contact;
motor acceleration;
a steady running cutting mechanism.

No body-contact sounds.

NO MUSIC.
NO DIALOGUE.

END PROMPT
